info.title: App AI Gateway API v2
info.description: A provider-native AI proxy for iOS applications and trusted server backends. Provider keys stay on the gateway; requests are checked, limited and recorded before they reach a provider.

servers.description: The cloud API host. On a self-hosted gateway, use your own origin.

tags.name: App sign-in
tags.description: App Attest challenges and keys, and exchanging a client proof for a gateway token.

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description: Polling a job submitted through the gateway, such as a fal queue job. Polls are free.

tags.name: Admin providers
tags.description: Provider connections and their keys. A key is write-only: only its hint is ever returned.

tags.name: Admin usage
tags.description: What your apps used and cost: totals for a month, per day and by dimension from day totals kept 400 days, and the charges themselves, kept 90 days.

tags.name: Admin diagnostics
tags.description: Why your apps' users cannot sign in or get answers: sign-in attempts, refused requests and a summary of both, kept 90 days.

tags.name: Admin access
tags.description: Who is calling, your accounts, management keys, and CLI and MCP sign-ins.

tags.name: Admin operations
tags.description: Writes an agent hands to a person: where each stands, and revealing a key one created.

tags.name: Console
tags.description: The console's own pages: OAuth consent, entering a CLI sign-in code, and approving a key an agent asked for. Called only from the console's origin.

GatewayBearer.description: A gateway access token from POST /v2/apps/{app}/auth/token, or an app key for a server app that signs no users in. On App Attest apps that sign every request, the request also carries X-AppAttest-Proof.

ManagementBearer.description: A management key, or an OAuth access token from the CLI's or an MCP client's sign-in. It acts for one account, with the read or manage grant it was issued with. Writes need the manage grant and an owner or admin role.

ConsoleSession.name: agw2_identity_auth.session_token
ConsoleSession.description: The console's sign-in. Management calls with it must also send x-console-request: 1. Console page calls must come from the console's own origin.

vault.description: Whether the key vault is set up: `ok`, or `misconfigured` when its settings are missing or invalid. No provider key can be opened while it is `misconfigured`. Optional: older deployments leave it out.

email.description: Whether the deployment can send verification email: `off` when no email is set up (addresses are not verified), `ok`, or `misconfigured` when it is meant to send but its settings are incomplete. Which setting is wrong is logged, never shown here. Optional: older deployments leave it out.

accepts_app_transaction.description: True when the token exchange accepts app_transaction. A client sends one, and signs over its hash, only when this says so.

data.description: Machine-readable facts about this refusal, present only where the code alone is not actionable. A rate_limited refusal carries scope, limit, windowSeconds, retryAfterSeconds and resetAt.

recorded.description: False when the challenge was never issued for this app, or was already spent or reported.

step.description: The step that failed after the challenge was issued: attest_key, generate_assertion, issuer_token, register or token.

domain.description: The error's domain, such as com.apple.devicecheck.error. Stored only when it is a short token (letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, at most 64 characters); anything else is stored as other.

The error's domain, such as com.apple.devicecheck.error. Stored only when it is a short token (letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, at most 64 characters); anything else is stored as other.

recovered.description: True when the app recovered by itself, such as by registering a new key. Recorded as client_recovered.

verify_on.description: On App Attest apps: every_request means every request sent with this token must carry X-AppAttest-Proof; token_exchange means requests carry only the token. Absent on other apps.

app_transaction.description: The App Store's signed AppTransaction (its JWS), which names the Apple Account the install belongs to. When present, the assertion signs client data that also carries app_transaction: the unpadded base64url SHA-256 of this string. One that does not verify names no account, and the install is counted on its own.

install_id.description: The App Attest key id of the install making the request, on App Attest apps. Null on server apps.

requests_today.description: Requests made so far in the current UTC day: by this install on an App Attest app, by this user on a server app. Null when the app sets no per-user limit, in which case requests are not counted.

requests_remaining.description: What is left of requests_per_day. Null when no daily limit is set.

requests_per_minute.description: The per-minute limit on each install (App Attest) or user (server). Null means unlimited.

requests_per_day.description: The per-day limit on each install (App Attest) or user (server). Null means unlimited.

monthly_cost_usd.description: Spent so far in the current UTC month against the budget below, by whoever budget_scope names.

monthly_budget_usd.description: The monthly budget on each Apple Account, install or user. Null means unlimited.

budget_scope.description: Whose month monthly_cost_usd is: apple_account, install or user.

blocked.description: Whether this user has been blocked in the console.

JobAnswer.description: The provider's own answer, with its links pointing at the gateway.

jwks_url.description: An https URL. Stored in the canonical form `URL` prints.
An https URL. Stored in the canonical form `URL` prints.

store.description: Keep a copy of every call this app sends through the gateway, request and response, with the media `keep` allows.

images.description: Keep images beside the conversation. Off, each is recorded by its type and size alone.

audio.description: Keep audio: recordings sent for transcription, audio in a request, spoken replies beside the conversation. Off, each is recorded by its type and size alone.

files.description: Keep every other attached file, such as a PDF or a text document beside the conversation. Off, each is recorded by its type and size alone.

retention_days.description: Days a stored conversation is kept before it is deleted.

warnings.description: Behaviour of this app that will stop on a stated date, worked out when the app is read; empty when there is none. Read-only: tell the person who owns the app, and act before each date. Absent on older gateways.

code.description: Stable identifier of what the warning is about.

message.description: What will stop, when, and what to do about it, in one sentence or two.

until.description: ISO 8601 UTC instant the behaviour stops.

providers.description: Every provider connection the app's routing or presets name, presets' fallbacks included. A disabled one is listed as disabled, and one that was deleted as missing, with a null id.

ready.description: `ready` means the app is active and at least one connection its routes or presets use can be reached: one that is active, or, for a preset, a first connection turned off with an active fallback. It checks connection status only, not that a request will serve: confirm with a real request, or the example requests.

limitations.description: What this check did not exercise, one sentence each.

installs.description: How many App Attest keys the user holds: one per install. Always 0 on server apps.

is_install.description: Whether this id is itself an App Attest key, so the row is one install.

is_virtual.description: True for a user id that only the app's usage or refusals name, such as a server app's end-user header. Such a user has no row, and cannot be blocked.

charges.description: Charges in the month, corrections not counted.

failed.description: Of those, attempts that did not end with success.

cost_nano.description: What the month cost, in nano-dollars, corrections included.

usage.description: The user's usage in `month`, from the ledger.

id.description: The job's id in the ledger.

submitted_at.description: When the job was submitted, ISO 8601.

estimate_nano.description: The estimate charged at submit, in nano-dollars; null when it has no price yet.

correction_nano.description: What the job's corrections added or removed, in nano-dollars; null when it has none.

total_nano.description: The estimate and its corrections together, in nano-dollars.

measured.description: How complete the usage is: the estimate's label until the job settles, then the settlement's.

state.description: `settled`: corrected to the provider's final figure. `checking`: the gateway still checks the job. `estimate_kept`: the provider gave no figure the price can use, so the estimate stays. `gave_up`: the job's result could not be read in time; the estimate stays.

settled_at.description: When the job was settled, ISO 8601.

next_check_at.description: While `checking`: when the gateway next checks the job, ISO 8601. A time well in the past means the check is overdue.

charges.description: Calls, session slices and job estimates. Corrections are not counted: they change the cost of a charge already counted.

failed.description: Of those, attempts that did not end with success.

unpriced.description: Of those, charges that still have no price: not priced yet, or a passthrough path with no price. Their cost counts as 0. Once a pricing correction prices one, its cost is added and it leaves this count. It may also count failed attempts that cost nothing, where the provider reports its own price and a failure reported none.

cost_nano.description: What it cost, in nano-dollars (1 = $0.000000001), corrections included.

cost_usd.description: The same cost in dollars, for display.

session_ms.description: Connection time of live sessions, in milliseconds.

apps.description: Every app with usage in the month, largest cost first. A deleted app keeps its usage, with a null name.

first_usage_day.description: The UTC day of the account's oldest usage still kept (YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM once it is only in month totals). Null when the account has never made a call.

owner_id.description: The call, session or job the charge belongs to.

corrects_charge_id.description: For a correction: the charge it corrects.

correction_kind.description: For a correction: units, dollars or pricing.

status.description: How the attempt ended: ok, provider_error, timeout, network_error or client_aborted. The list may grow.

model_author.description: Who made the model, from the price list or the model id, as v1. An analytics field only: it never affects prices or limits. Null when unknown.

price_is_estimate.description: The cost is not exact: a job's estimate, before its final figure corrects it, or the closest known price for a service mode with no exact one.

usage_day.description: The UTC day the charge counts on.

daily.description: Sign-in attempts per UTC day, by event, outcome and reason, oldest first.

failing_networks.description: The networks failed sign-in attempts came from, busiest first, at most ten. Attempts that recovered on their own, and those from an unknown network, are left out. Apple's own network (714) is where App Review tests apps.

failed_charges.description: Calls, session slices and job estimates per UTC day that did not end with success, from the usage totals.

rejection_samples.description: Sampled refusals before a provider was reached, per UTC day. Samples, not exact request totals.

success_rate.description: Null when the window has no exchanges at all, which is not a perfect score.

claim_delay.description: How long users waited for an entitlement claim to reach the issuer, for the waits that ended in the window.

pending_users.description: Active users waiting on an entitlement claim right now, counting waits that began within the last 90 days (as long as events are kept).

apple_failures.description: Failed sign-ins in the window from Apple's own network (714), where App Review tests apps, counted on their own so busier networks never hide them. Null when there were none; absent from older gateways.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next, older page; null on the last one.

outcome.description: ok, an error code, or a challenge outcome. The list may grow.

reason.description: A short token saying more, such as an issuer's rejection reason.

claim_delay_ms.description: For a sign-in that ended the user's wait for an entitlement claim: how long the wait was.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next, older page; null on the last one.

events.description: Newest first. Samples, not every refusal; kept 90 days.

reason.description: Why it was refused. The list may grow.

scope.description: Whose limit refused it, where a limit did: user, install, apple_account, app or account.

model.description: The requested model, when it names one the gateway knows; unrecognized otherwise.

name.description: The file's name within the app: `<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-<batch>.jsonl.gz`.

records.description: How many calls the file holds, one per line.

uploaded_at.description: When the file was written, ISO 8601.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last one.

reason.description: Why the key was not confirmed. no_probe: this provider has no cheap call to test with. unreachable: no answer in time. unexpected_status: an answer that proves nothing either way. rejected: the provider refused the key with 401. Usually the key is wrong, but some providers answer 401 for a key restricted so it cannot list models.

status.description: The provider's HTTP status, for unexpected_status and rejected.

verificationPending.description: True while this account's apps are refused (`email_unverified`) because no owner has verified their email address yet. Only where the deployment verifies addresses; left out otherwise.

planName.description: The plan's name; null when no plan resolves or billing cannot be read.

used.description: Requests sent to providers in this period, across all apps.

resetAt.description: When the allowance resets; the same as periodEnd.

allowance.description: This period's requests against the plan's allowance; null when the plan sets no monthly limit or it cannot be read.

billing.description: The account's plan and this period's request allowance. Only on a hosted deployment with billing; left out otherwise.

status.description: `sent` when a link went out now; `already_verified` when the address needs none.

email.description: The address the link was sent to, or that is already verified.

returnTo.description: A console path to continue at once the link is opened, such as `/v2/apps`.
The console path the link was asked for from, to continue there; null for none.

token.description: The `token` in the `#` fragment of the link in the verification email: the page reads it there and posts it here, so it never reaches a request log.

put.description: Asks the provider to cancel a job submitted through the gateway, and passes its answer on. A cancelled job ends in one of three ways, whether it is cancelled here or at the provider directly: a queued job the provider confirms with no billed units costs nothing; a cancel or failure the provider bills is charged at the job's saved rate, by the reported units or as one job for a flat price per job; and if the provider's billed units cannot be read, the estimate stays. Free: it uses no request limit and no plan allowance.

post.summary: Create an app
post.description: Send `name`, `config` and an optional `status`. The gateway assigns the id: the name made URL-safe plus a random suffix. Every provider connection, operation and model the config names is checked, and a model with no price is refused with `pricing_not_configured`. An app-key app gets its first key, shown once as `api_key`.

patch.description: Applies `operations` in order to the app as `getApp` answers it, then saves the result exactly as `PUT` would: the same checks, the same errors, and nothing written unless every operation applies and the result is accepted. Each operation is RFC 6902 `add`, `replace` or `remove` at a JSON Pointer under `/name`, `/status` or `/config`, for example `{"op": "replace", "path": "/config/limits/per_app/requests/per_minute", "value": 600}`. A value is written as given: `null` sets a limit to unlimited, and only `remove` deletes. Needs `revision`, as `PUT` does. An operation that cannot apply answers `400 invalid_request` naming its index.

post.description: Judged as an update of this app would be. After a provider connection is deleted, an edit may keep that connection's routing entry only if the entry is unchanged; an added or changed entry for it is refused. Needs only the read grant: nothing is saved.

get.summary: Check whether an app is ready to serve requests
get.description: Checks the stored config as an update would, and lists every provider connection its routes and presets name, with its status (a disabled one as disabled, a deleted one as missing). `ready` means the app is active and at least one connection its routes or presets use can be reached: one that is active, or, for a preset, a first connection turned off with an active fallback. It checks connection status only, not that a request will serve: confirm with a real request, or the example requests. It sends no provider request, and `limitations` says what it did not try. A stored config that would no longer be accepted answers `400` with the reason.

get.summary: List the tools the CLI builds its commands from
get.description: The MCP server's tools, each with the command `agw` offers it as, the input fields it takes positionally, and how its result is shown. The CLI keeps this list and builds every command it does not implement itself from it, so a tool added to the gateway is a command of every installed CLI without a release. The list is the same for every caller of one deployment, so it needs no credential.

200.description: The tools and the revision that names this list.

post.summary: Run one tool, as the CLI does
post.description: Runs one MCP tool with the arguments in the body, through the same operations, authorization and refusals as an MCP `tools/call`: a read needs any credential, and a change needs what that change needs over the API. A refusal is an HTTP error with the gateway's error code. Every answer, a refusal included, carries the list's revision in `Agw-Tools-Revision`; a CLI holding another one fetches the list again. Send the tool's `guard` from your list in `Agw-Tool-Guard`: when it differs from the tool's current one, the call is refused with `409 tool_changed` before anything runs.

schema.description: The tool's name, as listCliTools returns it.

parameters.description: The tool's name, as listCliTools returns it.
parameters.name: tool

200.description: The tool's structured result and its one-line summary.

401.description: A valid management key, OAuth token or console sign-in is required.

403.description: The credential has only the read grant, or its owner is not an account owner or admin. A console tab naming an account the person is not a member of (`x-account-id`) is refused with `account_forbidden`.

404.description: `tool_not_found`: this deployment has no tool of that name. Any other code: what the tool names does not exist.

409.description: `tool_changed`: the tool has become destructive or needs more of the CLI since the caller's list; nothing ran. Otherwise the change conflicts with the current state.

post.summary: Email verification: send a link
post.description: Sends a verification link to the address of the person signed in to this browser, for their console session only. Where the deployment verifies email addresses, an account's apps serve requests only once an owner has verified theirs; reading and changing settings never waits for it. A link lasts 24 hours, and a sign-up with a password sends the first one itself. Counted per person.

200.description: Whether a link went out, and to which address.

401.description: No person is signed in to this browser (`session_required`).

403.description: The request did not come from the console's own page.

404.description: Not served here (only on the console's origin).

409.description: This deployment does not verify email addresses, or the sign-in has no address of its own (`conflict`).

429.description: Too many links were sent for this sign-in. Carries Retry-After.

503.description: The deployment could not send the email (`email_unavailable`).

post.summary: Email verification: confirm a link
post.description: Verifies the address a verification link was sent to. The link alone is the proof, so no sign-in is needed; it is bound to the sign-in and the address it was sent for, and stops working once it expires or the address changes. Confirming a link again answers the same.

200.description: The address verified, and where to continue.

400.description: The link is malformed, has expired, or no longer matches the sign-in's address (`invalid_request`).

403.description: The request did not come from the console's own page.

404.description: Not served here (only on the console's origin).
